From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: DeepProbe: post-demo recap + AB lab plan (latency & throughput focus)

Hi Nihar / team —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a proposed A/B lab plan so we can close the competitive questions vs Hyperscaler-A and Hyperscaler-B:

Summary from the call:
- You care most about p95/p99 latency at target payloads, and steady tokens/sec under concurrency (10, 50, 200 concurrent users).
- Hyperscaler-A showed lower median but had p99 spikes during burst; Hyperscaler-B has more consistent p95 but worse tokens/sec.
- Key success criteria for you: p99 < 350ms for 95% of requests at 50 concurrency and baseline throughput >= 4k tokens/sec at steady state.

Proposed AB lab (attached: deepprobe-bench-plan-v1.pdf):
1) Workloads: three profiles (short chat msgs ~50 tokens, medium 256 tokens, long 1024 tokens)
2) Concurrency sweep: 10 / 50 / 200 users; run 15-minute windows to capture steady-state and microburst behavior
3) Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, failed requests, KV cache hit rates, GPU utilization.
4) Comparators: your Hyperscaler export (you’ve shared baseline logs), Hyperscaler-A public instance, and Redwood Dedicated + quantized 4-bit variant.
5) Controlled A/B: Redwood will run side-by-side with the Hyperscaler snapshots we discussed — identical prompts, pinned seeds, same model family where possible.

Ask for the next step:
- Can you confirm the three payload profiles and the sample traffic generator we should use? (We can use your existing harness or ours: https://github.com/redwood/deepprobe-harness)
- Please share a 24-hour window when your infra can allow in-bound test traffic (we usually need a 2–3 hour reserved slot).

Internal note: Neha/Rachel — see the attached plan. I tagged out the variant list; we should include a quantized run + an NVLink-enabled run. Please respond with availability and a short list of configs you need from ACME.

Thanks,
Jordan
vp-sales@redwood.ai | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DeepProbe: post-demo recap + AB lab plan (latency & throughput focus)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications before we lock a window:
- Workloads: the 256-token and 1024-token profiles look good. For the 50-token profile can you include a short multi-turn chat (3 turns) to simulate real user back-and-forth?
- Baselines: we will provide Hyperscaler-A and Hyperscaler-B exported traces but need to confirm their exact model variants (we’ll send a CSV).
- Who will orchestrate the A/B switch? Do you need us to accept traffic from Redwood IP ranges, or will you spin up instances in our VPC (preferred)?
- Data/Logs: we require request-level anonymization and an NDA addendum for log access. Can you confirm Redwood’s log retention and masking defaults?

If we can get those answers, I’ll propose two windows (early next week).

— Nihar
Nihar Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Systems
nihar@acme.com

Forwarding Nihar’s questions — quick internal plan and owners:

- Workload tweak: add a 3-turn short-chat variant for the 50-token profile (Rachel: please script turns + seed messages).
- Baselines: ACME will share CSV of model variants. Neha: we’ll map Hyperscaler models to closest Redwood-verified variants; include fallback mapping logic.
- Orchestration: prefer to run tests in ACME VPC for fidelity. Neha, can you draft the minimal infra checklist (incoming IPs, ports, test harness container image) and note whether we need a temporary service account?
- Logs & compliance: Rachel, please outline what fields we need for p95/p99 analysis and propose a masking plan (PII removal + hashed ids). Also prepare a one-paragraph NDA addendum we can send to ACME legal.

Timeline: target early next week (Mon/Tue) for a reserved 3-hour window. If ACME cannot host, we can run from our Dedicated pool but with slightly reduced fidelity for NVLink tests.

Jordan

Jordan / Rachel —

I can take infra ownership for the ACME-hosted run. Notes and constraints below: 

Planned infra checklist:
- Test harness: use deepprobe-harness container (link in thread). Need ACME to whitelist our runner IP ranges: 34.120.11.0/24 and 34.120.12.0/24.
- Service account: temporary svc-deepprobe@redwood-sa with scoped read-only token — ACME to provision if they want VPC-native.
- Metrics collection: Prometheus + Grafana; I’ll push a dashboard template and a metrics mapping table.
- Autoscaling config: for 200 concurrent users we need burst capacity; suggest a warm-up ramp (5 min) before measurement window to stabilize cache + batching.
- Data policy: Redwood defaults: 30-day retention for request metadata, 7-day retention for raw request bodies when provided. We will apply field-level masking (email, IP) and hash user IDs; happy to add a short NDA addendum.

I’ll assemble a minimal runbook and upload it to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123-bench-config) by EOD. Tentative lab window: Mon 2029-06-03 09:00–12:00 PT.

Neha
